keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 619-620: the northern Shanxi land plus Taiyuan, 'Li Yuan's initial power base', which he 'briefly captured... in 619' (the Transition page: he took 'much of modern Shanxi, which Tang had controlled').

region.text: 'modern northern Shanxi and parts of central Inner Mongolia' (the page), as a radius round Datong

ledger.note: 617: Liu Wuzhou kills Wang and rises. 'In spring 617, he took his men to the commandery government and killed Wang'; the Eastern Turk Ashina Duojishi created him Dingyang Khan (era Tianxing 617-620). The page names no month.
619: Liu takes Taiyuan. He 'briefly captured Li Yuan's initial power base of Taiyuan in 619' and moved his capital there from Mayi (the page does not date the move).
619: the capital moves from Mayi to Taiyuan (undated on the page; placed at the capture).

union.text: 'modern northern Shanxi and parts of central Inner Mongolia' (the page), as a radius round Datong

ledger.note: 620: Li Shimin crushes the Dingyang. 'In summer 620, Li Shimin... launched a major counterattack'; Liu 'abandoned Taiyuan in panic and fled to Eastern Tujue'; 'his Dingyang state was integrated into Tang' (Transition page).

wars.name: Tang campaign against Liu Wuzhou
wars.outcome: Tang victory in summer 620; Liu fled to the Eastern Turks and was executed there (probably August 622).
wars.note: The footnotes disagree: 620 in the Old Book of Tang, 622 in the New Book for Liu's death.

certainty.note: A frontier region between the Tang and the Eastern Turks; the page gives regions, no boundary.

sources.title: Liu Wuzhou
sources.note: Spring 617 rising, Dingyang Khan, northern Shanxi and Inner Mongolia, Taiyuan 619, Li Shimin's summer 620 counterattack, flight and death.

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang
sources.note: Dingyang 'by 617' to summer 620, in northern Shanxi; 'integrated into Tang'.

notes: REBEL STATE. The Eastern Turks' dossier (ia-01) should record the Dingyang as their vassal ('created him Dingyang Khan'); this dossier does not. Liu Wuzhou's Han/Dingyang state name is not given on the page. Mayi's identification with Shuozhou is the researcher's.
